rv.q: It's a zesty little piece that certainly makes good on its thesis that nobody ever leaves the traumas of middle school behind.
"Veal" takes the idea of nostalgia and stretches it to the most absurd limits.
It is a must see if you are up for a wild ride of great theatre.
“Veal” is a perfectly cast, brilliantly acted and genuinely chilling story of cruelty, madness and revenge.
Jojo Jones’ World Premiere is extremely interesting and highly entertaining.
Imagination and a strong authorial voice are in much shorter supply.
Brown and Chopson are hypnotic in their confrontations with each other.
The subject of “Veal” is completely absorbing, every now and then I found myself thinking of current events and another despot who rules by whim, and loves to surround himself with sycophants.
One thing is for sure, Veal is an excellently written and performed show by all the cast.
Veal is a twisted, dark, can’t take your eyes away tale of retribution, power, and the wolf that lives in us all.
This is a 90 minute show with no intermission that will hold your interest from start to finish, and the ending will surprise many of you.

cn.t: Critics praise this darkly twisted psychological thriller about middle school bullying and revenge in a dystopian setting, calling it challenging, terrifying, and darkly funny—the kind of provocative theater A Red Orchid does best.
